description: Change an audio clip's speed, pitch, formants, or warp anchors in one undoable edit. Get clip_index and expected_revision from audio_clips_list. Omitted fields keep their current values. Set stretch_to to resize and scale the clip together, like Alt-dragging its right edge. Supply stretch or stretch_to, never both. Varispeed links pitch to speed like tape. Clear pitch, formant, preserve_formants and warp_markers when switching to varispeed. Other edits keep the timeline range fixed. Stretch is output duration divided by source duration; explicit tempo_follow=true instead fits the whole source to the clip range and clears its source offset and loop. Do not supply stretch together with tempo_follow=true; a processing mode is required. Unrelated edits that omit tempo_follow preserve existing trim/loop settings. Pitch and formant are in semitones. Set preserve_formants to compensate for pitch-induced formant movement. Compare the same window with audition_range.

description: Search several external sample markets at once for drum one-shots, loops, vocals, FX and instrument phrases. This build is a client: it hosts no catalogue. Markets with local debug plugins: openverse (an aggregator over Freesound, Jamendo, Wikimedia and others; no key), wikimedia-commons (no key), internet-archive (no key), freesound (needs FREESOUND_API_KEY or the org.opencompose.samples/freesound keyring item; a Freesound OAuth2 connection in External Sources preferences pulls the original, otherwise the 128 kbps preview), jamendo (needs JAMENDO_CLIENT_ID or the jamendo keyring item). Looperman, Splice, SampleSwap, SoundBible, Mixkit, Pixabay, Sample Focus, Bedroom Producers Blog and Cymatics are reported as unavailable with the reason and are never scraped. Each item carries its provider, id, kind, duration, licence, credit line and license_ok: CC0, public domain, CC BY and CC BY-SA need no confirmation; non-commercial, no-derivatives, GFDL and community licences are free to pull once the caller passes accept_licence to sample_pull. Every requested market appears in the providers array with available and reason, even when it could not answer, and a failing market is reported per page. Paged: pass next_offset back as offset. description: Analyze and transcribe an external audio file or stem into notes: note events (start, end, MIDI number, name, cents off that pitch, detector confidence) with one monophonic detector; prefer writing the notes from what you hear, and use this only for audio whose notes are not written in the project DSL and that you cannot transcribe reliably by ear. Note times are relative to `start`, and the window may be a section. Every note also carries `start_beat` (quarter-note beats from the window start, 0-based), `duration_beats`, `bar` (1-based) and `suggested_duration`, the nearest DSL token (w, h, q, 8th, 16th, 32nd, 64th, dotted or triplet). Derive the duration token from `suggested_duration`; do not invent one. An octave is only decided when it beats the other octave by 6 dB on its own fundamental: a note whose sub-octave or octave-up layer is that close carries `octave_ambiguous: true` and `octave_runner_up` (the MIDI number it would take instead), and a repeated pitch holds its earlier octave while the reading stays ambiguous. When a note you need is flagged, do not pick an octave from it — re-run on a window where that voice sounds alone (or a stem), and say which octave you could not pin down. The top level reports the grid the beats assume (`tempo_bpm`, `time_signature`, `beats_per_bar`, `beat_seconds`, `quantise` tolerance); it comes from the tempo/time_signature arguments, else this WAV's render metadata, else the `project` you pass, and only then the engine default 120 BPM 4/4 with a warning. If the external tempo is unknown, ask audio_analyze for beat_grid evidence before supplying a confirmed grid. A note more than `quantise` beats off the 1/16 grid is named in `warnings` and its suggestion is a guess. A chord sets `polyphonic: true` and only the strongest voice is transcribed; drums, chords and ornaments under about 50 ms are not. Use `audition_range` to hear the same window.

description: Compare two audio files (WAV or supported compressed media such as MP3/FLAC) using shared comparison definitions: LUFS delta, per-octave and body deltas, envelope and waveform correlation, max sample difference, level-matched log-mel error, tilt, crest/attack, bass harmonics and headline score. Compressed media is decoded to stereo at its native sample rate. Both analyzed signals must share a sample rate and frame count; render both sides at the same rate, which is the app's current output rate (Preferences → Audio). Different lengths or sample rates are refused unless allow_mismatch=true. For a passage, specify duration (up to 30 seconds) and independent reference_start and candidate_start in source seconds. A passage must fit both files. Set listen=true with a 0.4–8 second passage to receive two level-matched listening copies when measurable. They preserve source timing; the report verifies the actual delivered PCM. The listening comparison is labeled, so it is open rather than blind.
